Interface MailboxFactory

All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultMailboxFactory
public interface MailboxFactory
Factory for constructing and connecting to Mailbox instances.

Two families of operations are provided:

  • create — eagerly provisions a mailbox in the backing store. This performs backend I/O and establishes the mailbox's TTL. Creating a mailbox with an existing name replaces it: create is last-write-wins, and the TTL passed here supersedes any previously configured TTL for that name.
  • connect — returns a handle to an existing mailbox without performing backend I/O at factory call time. The first deliver or subscribe operation (Mailbox.deliver(T) or Mailbox.subscribe()) probes the backend once: if no mailbox exists at name, that first operation throws MailboxNotFoundException. Mailbox.delete() does not probe and remains a retry-safe no-op when the mailbox is already gone. Once the one-shot probe passes, subsequent operations behave exactly as they would on a create-sourced handle — terminal-state transitions surface as MailboxExpiredException in the normal way.

  • Method Details

    • create

      <T> Mailbox<T> create(String name, Class<T> type, Duration ttl)
      Create a new mailbox with the given name and value type.

      If a mailbox with name already exists, it is replaced: create is last-write-wins, and the ttl passed here supersedes any previously configured TTL for that name.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the mailbox value type
      Parameters:
      name - the logical name for the mailbox
      type - the value type class
      ttl - how long the mailbox lives before expiring automatically; must be strictly positive
      Returns:
      a newly provisioned mailbox
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is zero or negative, or exceeds the maximum allowed duration
